Messages.Body:
Can anyone speak about their experience with this product or this player?

franciscodroid.blogspot.com/2011/03/primeiro-aplicativo-no-android-market.html

Primeiro aplicativo no Android Market!
Olá, pessoal!

Consegui colocar o primeiro aplicativo no Android Market: VampiDroid Cards Reference. Para baixar, basta acessar esse link para o Android Market.

O que é o VampiDroid?

O VampiDroid foi inspirado na ideia de servir de referência para obter informações sobre as cartas do jogo: VTES - Vampire: The Eternal Struggle

Eu e meus amigos jogamos muito esse jogo e eu pensei que ter mais essa fonte de informação disponível à mão no celular seria bastante interessante e útil.

Nessa primeira versão já estão disponíveis algumas funcionalidades interessantes. Você já pode:

* ver a listagem de todas as cartas;
* fazer pesquisa pelo nome;
* ver o conteúdo da carta (disciplinas, texto, requisitos, etc)

Para as próximas versões estou planejando implementar a ideia do meu amigo Osny que é permitir a criação, importação e exportação de decks. Dessa maneira o jogador vai poder criar novos decks e catalogá-los além de poder importar os catálogos já criados por outros jogadores.

Além dessa ideia, estou pensando também em implementar muitas maneiras de fazer ordenação das cartas. Assim, o jogador poderá ver cartas ordenadas por disciplina, clã, custo, e vários outros critérios.

---

Hi!

I just wanted to let you know that I'm working in a utility for VTES
to Android platform called VampiDroid.

You can check it out from any Android phone through Android Market.

Here is a link: market.android.com/details?id=name.vampidroid

Please, let me know what do you think.

Thanks in advance.

--
Regards,

Messages.Author: cmdrKEEN
Messages.Body:
I have that app on my phone for some time now. Its a simple programm, that searches the database on the device (no internet connection needed) by cardname. Its useful to check the actual wording of a card, but not much more as you cant filter or search by group or cost or anything.

If you have a internet connection (and if you have a android phone you most probably have that) you could use secretlibrary or other pages, that have a lot more options. May also be useful if you travel to other countries to avoid roaming charges.

All in all its no program you will use regulary but it has its uses in specific situations or to put in jyhad vocabulary: its rather conditional.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Search Functionalities:

- Multi-criterium filter for crypt.
dom+ AND for+
Ventrue AND obf+

- Group filter for crypt
G5
G4-6

- Crypt / Discipline requirements on the same line in library pannel (rather than having empty lines). Or don't display empty lines.

- "Advanced" filters:
"Anarch", "Black Hand", ... (especially for library requirements)

Deckbuilding, Have&Want
Add the "Add to decklist" / "Add to Have list" / "Add to Want list"
=> "See decklist", "Send decklist to secretLibrary", "share decklist via email/...", "See Wantlist"

Medium-term:
"See rulings" option when a card is selected.

Long-term (because probably difficult to store): "View image"

EDIT:
Crypt filters could be a poppup rather than a small "dropdown list"

Fields would then be:

Discipline : [if filled, add a new "Discpline" line, and a "OR" or an "AND" checkbox]
Sect:
Clan:
Capacity: (range allowed)
Group: (range allowed)

It's probably OK to skip imbueds in a first part.

For crypt cards:
Type:
Clan / Discpline requirement: (Forced March should match the "for" requirement)
Blood / Pool cost: (range allowed)
Special: Anarch / Black Hand / Seraph / Infernal / Flight / ...

It's probably OK to skip the Special in a first part.
